Introduction:
**0:** The generated section covers the closed-book exam framing, hallucination risk, fine-tuning limitations, and context-window limitations (with an unusually detailed academic framing) with the same substance as the expected section. However, unlike the reduced-but-still-present agentic-RAG preview seen in an earlier replicate (not penalized there, since the essential idea was still grasped), this section contains no mention at all of the agentic-RAG angle — not even a brief gesture toward "advanced and agentic patterns." The expected section's dedicated paragraph introducing "Agentic RAG" as a concept and term (exposing the knowledge base as a tool, referencing Lessons 6 and 8) has no counterpart here whatsoever. Per ruling, a complete absence of this idea is distinct from — and does not benefit from — the standing allowance for reduced-detail coverage, so this is scored as a genuine omission.

The RAG System: Core Components:
**1:** Both sections cover the same three pillars — Retrieval, Augmentation, and Generation — with matching substance and no notable omissions.

The RAG Pipeline: Ingestion and Retrieval:
**0:** Both sections cover the same two-phase structure with matching substance for each step, and both reference Lesson 4's structured outputs. The generated section's code example is a valid addition, not an omission. However, as in every replicate of this lesson graded so far, two ideas present in the expected section are absent: (1) the callout on long-context/asymmetric-search embedding models; (2) the guidance on tuning chunk size empirically against retrieval metrics (hit rate/recall, MRR@k, nDCG@k) and the specific chunk-size/overlap ranges. These remain substantive, non-trivial ideas in the expected section with no equivalent here.

Advanced RAG Techniques:
**1:** Both sections cover the same six techniques — Hybrid Search, Re-ranking, Query Transformations, Advanced Chunking, GraphRAG, and Metadata Filtering — with matching substance. The generated section's added statistics and context (the enterprise-search low-signal note, the HyDE latency finding, the university-slides chunking case study, the Graphiti bitemporal citation) are additions rather than omissions and don't affect the core ideas, which are otherwise complete.

Agentic RAG:
**1:** Both sections cover the standard-vs-agentic distinction, the ReAct-loop tie-in, and — unlike two of the three previous replicates — all four agentic capabilities: iterative refinement, dynamic source selection, information fusion, and the knowledge-base-update capability correctly previewed toward Lesson 10 ("an agent can even decide to update its knowledge base with new information it learns"). The same Thought/Action/Observation worked example is present. The generated section's added self-critique/reflection mechanism is an addition rather than an omission.

Conclusion:
**1:** Both sections cover the same key takeaways: RAG as the primary industry solution to the LLM knowledge problem, the necessity of advanced techniques for production quality, the agentic future of retrieval, the three core benefits, RAG's status as a foundational competency and subset of Context Engineering, and the same transition preview into Lesson 10 plus future topics.
